en.greeting: Hi, welcome to C1 reading! Today you read like a careful professional: academic abstracts, the small print in contracts, and arguments that try to persuade you. Let's start!

steps.title: Specialised texts have a map
steps.text: At B2 you skimmed for the gist, scanned for one fact and read between the lines. Specialised texts need all three, plus a map.
steps.body:
**Academic paper**: read the **title** and the **abstract**, then the **conclusion**, then only the sections you need.
An **abstract** has four parts:
- **Aim**: This study examines…
- **Method**: We surveyed… / Data were collected from…
- **Findings**: Results show… / We found that…
- **Limitation**: However, the study only… / The results may not apply to…
An **executive summary** = a whole business report on one page, usually ending with **recommendations**. Read it first.

steps.title: Which part of the abstract?
steps.text: Here's an abstract from an education journal. Look for the signal words in each sentence.

question.prompt: Read the abstract: '(1) This study investigates whether a vocabulary app helps first-year university students. (2) 240 students were split into two groups for one semester. (3) Students who used the app daily raised their vocabulary scores by 11%, compared with 4% in the other group. (4) However, the study lasted only one semester.' Which part is sentence (3)?
question.explanation: Sentence (3) gives the **results**, with numbers (11% compared with 4%): that's the **findings**. Sentence (2) is the method (how the study was done), and sentence (4), after **However**, is the limitation.

steps.title: Terms and conditions: the small print
steps.text: Now a text most people never read until it costs them money: the terms and conditions of an e-wallet or a phone contract.
steps.body:
Scan for the **money** and the **dates** (fee, Rp, refund, cancel, renew, days), then read those clauses word by word.
- **renews automatically unless you cancel** = if you do nothing, you pay again
- **subject to** = only if a condition is met
- **at our sole discretion** = only the company decides
- **notwithstanding clause 4** = even though clause 4 says something else, this rule wins
- **you agree to** = you accept it or promise it
**Trap:** in T&Cs, **We may…** means *we have the right to* (berhak), not *mungkin*.

steps.title: Which clause wins?
steps.text: Here are two clauses from an e-wallet's terms. Read both before you answer: the second one changes the first.

options: Yes, because she asked within 7 days.
No, because clause 5.4 wins over clause 5.1.
Yes, but only half of it.
question.prompt: Read: '5.1 You can ask for a full refund of a top-up within 7 days. 5.4 Notwithstanding clause 5.1, top-ups made with a promo code are non-refundable.' Rina topped up Rp200,000 with a promo code three days ago. Can she get her money back?
question.explanation: **Notwithstanding clause 5.1** means: even though 5.1 allows refunds within 7 days, this rule wins. Rina used a promo code, so her top-up is **non-refundable**. The 7 days in 5.1 is the trap, and nothing in the text mentions half a refund.

steps.title: The shape of an argument
steps.text: At B2 you wrote arguments yourself. Now you take other writers' arguments apart and label each part.
steps.body:
- **Claim**: the main point (I believe…, …should…)
- **Reasons**: why (because, since, The main reason is…)
- **Evidence**: facts, numbers, examples that show it's true (According to…, A survey of… found…, For example…)
- **Counter-argument**: the other side (Some argue that…, Critics say…, Admittedly…)
- **Rebuttal**: the writer's answer (However…, But this ignores…, Yet…)
- **Conclusion**: the claim again (Therefore…, For these reasons…)
A **reason** says why; **evidence** shows it's true. Don't take the counter-argument as the writer's view.

steps.title: Reason or evidence?
steps.text: Find the signal words, then decide: is the sentence saying why, or showing that it's true?

question.prompt: Read: '(A) Hospitals should shorten night shifts. (B) Tired nurses make more mistakes, because they get too little sleep. (C) At one hospital in Medan, night nurses made twice as many medicine errors as day nurses last year. (D) Critics say shorter shifts cost more.' Which part of the argument is sentence (C)?
question.explanation: Sentence (C) gives a **fact with a number** from a real place: it shows that reason (B) is true, so it's **evidence**. (B) is the reason (it says **why**, with **because**), and (D), with **Critics say**, is the counter-argument.

steps.title: Spotting bias
steps.text: A text can contain only true facts and still be biased. The bias is in the words and in the choice of facts.
steps.body:
**Bias** = the writer leans to one side. Six signs:
- **Loaded words**: a **reckless** plan (negative) / a **bold** plan (positive) / a new plan (neutral); slashed vs reduced; claims vs says
- **One-sided evidence**: only the facts that help
- **Who funded it**: a sugar company's study says sugar is safe
- **Cherry-picked numbers**: only the best month
- **Small samples**: we asked 15 users
- **Appeal to authority**: a famous actor says it works; "experts agree" (which experts?)

steps.title: Make it neutral
steps.text: Now rewrite a biased sentence in neutral words. Drop the judgement, keep the facts.

question.solution: The plan will reduce funding for libraries.
question.prompt: Read: 'The reckless plan will slash funding for libraries.' Arrange the words to give the same facts in neutral words.
question.explanation: **reckless** (a negative judgement) disappears, and **slash** (cut a lot, carelessly) becomes the neutral **reduce**. The facts stay the same: a plan, and less money for libraries.

steps.title: Reading critically
steps.text: Last skill: does the evidence really support the claim? A critical reader asks questions before believing.
steps.body:
- **Correlation ≠ causation**: umbrella sales and dengue cases both rise in the rainy season. Umbrellas don't cause dengue: the rain causes both.
- **Sample**: how many people, and who? 15 friends ≠ all Indonesians.
- **What's missing?** Compared with what? The other months? Side effects?
- **Fact or opinion?** A fact can be checked; an opinion is a judgement.
Ask: **Who wrote it? For whom? Who paid? What's left out?** "A study shows…" isn't proof: one study only suggests.

steps.title: Is that the whole story?
steps.text: A city press release. Read the headline, then ask: is this number the whole story?

options: It uses only the best week, so the number may be cherry-picked.
40,000 passengers is too small a sample.
question.prompt: Read: 'NEW BUS LINE A HUGE SUCCESS. In its best week, during the school holidays, Bandung's new Line 9 carried 40,000 passengers. The city had planned for 30,000 a week.' The city hasn't published the numbers for the other weeks. What is the main problem with the evidence?
question.explanation: The writer chose **the best week**, in the holidays, and the other weeks are **missing**: a typical cherry-picked number. 40,000 passengers isn't a small sample, and the text doesn't say that one thing causes another.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's a cheat sheet to keep next to your next report, contract or opinion piece.

steps.text: Want more practice? A C1 article from British Council LearnEnglish that asks whether the statistics support our view of the world, and a Crash Course video on telling strong evidence from weak.

id.greeting: Hai, selamat datang di membaca level C1! Hari ini kamu membaca seperti profesional yang teliti: abstrak akademik, tulisan kecil di kontrak, dan argumen yang mencoba meyakinkanmu. Ayo mulai!

steps.title: Teks khusus punya peta
steps.text: Di B2 kamu sudah skimming untuk menangkap inti, scanning untuk satu fakta, dan membaca yang tersirat. Teks khusus butuh ketiganya, ditambah sebuah peta.
steps.body:
**Paper akademik**: baca **judul** dan **abstrak**, lalu **kesimpulan**, lalu hanya bagian yang kamu perlukan.
**Abstrak** punya empat bagian:
- **Aim** (tujuan): This study examines…
- **Method** (metode): We surveyed… / Data were collected from…
- **Findings** (temuan): Results show… / We found that…
- **Limitation** (keterbatasan): However, the study only… / The results may not apply to…
**Executive summary** (ringkasan eksekutif) = seluruh laporan bisnis dalam satu halaman, biasanya diakhiri **recommendations** (rekomendasi). Baca ini dulu.

steps.title: Bagian abstrak yang mana?
steps.text: Ini abstrak dari sebuah jurnal pendidikan. Cari kata penanda di setiap kalimat.

question.prompt: Baca abstraknya: '(1) This study investigates whether a vocabulary app helps first-year university students. (2) 240 students were split into two groups for one semester. (3) Students who used the app daily raised their vocabulary scores by 11%, compared with 4% in the other group. (4) However, the study lasted only one semester.' Kalimat (3) bagian yang mana?
question.explanation: Kalimat (3) memberi **hasil**, dengan angka (11% dibandingkan 4%): itu **findings** (temuan). Kalimat (2) adalah metode (bagaimana penelitiannya dilakukan), dan kalimat (4), setelah **However**, adalah keterbatasan (limitation).

steps.title: Syarat dan ketentuan: tulisan kecilnya
steps.text: Sekarang teks yang hampir tidak pernah dibaca orang sampai mereka rugi uang: syarat dan ketentuan dompet digital atau kontrak HP.
steps.body:
Scan **uang** dan **tanggal**-nya (fee, Rp, refund, cancel, renew, days), lalu baca klausul itu kata demi kata.
- **renews automatically unless you cancel** = kalau kamu diam saja, kamu bayar lagi
- **subject to** = hanya kalau syaratnya dipenuhi
- **at our sole discretion** = hanya perusahaan yang memutuskan
- **notwithstanding clause 4** = walaupun klausul 4 berkata lain, aturan inilah yang berlaku
- **you agree to** = kamu menerima atau menjanjikannya
**Jebakan:** di S&K, **We may…** artinya *kami berhak*, bukan *mungkin*.

steps.title: Klausul mana yang menang?
steps.text: Ini dua klausul dari syarat sebuah dompet digital. Baca keduanya sebelum menjawab: klausul kedua mengubah yang pertama.

options: Yes, because she asked within 7 days.
No, because clause 5.4 wins over clause 5.1.
Yes, but only half of it.
question.prompt: Baca: '5.1 You can ask for a full refund of a top-up within 7 days. 5.4 Notwithstanding clause 5.1, top-ups made with a promo code are non-refundable.' Tiga hari lalu Rina top-up Rp200.000 dengan kode promo. Bisakah uangnya kembali?
question.explanation: **Notwithstanding clause 5.1** artinya: walaupun 5.1 membolehkan refund dalam 7 hari, aturan inilah yang berlaku. Rina memakai kode promo, jadi top-up-nya **non-refundable** (tidak dapat dikembalikan). Angka 7 hari di 5.1 adalah jebakannya, dan teksnya tidak menyebut refund setengah sama sekali.
displayOptions: Ya, karena ia meminta dalam 7 hari.

steps.title: Bentuk sebuah argumen
steps.text: Di B2 kamu menulis argumen sendiri. Sekarang kamu membongkar argumen penulis lain dan memberi label pada setiap bagiannya.
steps.body:
- **Claim** (klaim): poin utama (I believe…, …should…)
- **Reasons** (alasan): mengapa (because, since, The main reason is…)
- **Evidence** (bukti): fakta, angka, contoh yang menunjukkan bahwa itu benar (According to…, A survey of… found…, For example…)
- **Counter-argument** (argumen tandingan): pendapat pihak lain (Some argue that…, Critics say…, Admittedly…)
- **Rebuttal** (bantahan): jawaban penulis (However…, But this ignores…, Yet…)
- **Conclusion** (kesimpulan): klaimnya lagi (Therefore…, For these reasons…)
**Alasan** menjawab mengapa; **bukti** menunjukkan bahwa itu benar. Jangan anggap argumen tandingan sebagai pendapat penulis.

steps.title: Alasan atau bukti?
steps.text: Cari kata penandanya, lalu putuskan: apakah kalimat itu menjawab mengapa, atau menunjukkan bahwa itu benar?

question.prompt: Baca: '(A) Hospitals should shorten night shifts. (B) Tired nurses make more mistakes, because they get too little sleep. (C) At one hospital in Medan, night nurses made twice as many medicine errors as day nurses last year. (D) Critics say shorter shifts cost more.' Kalimat (C) bagian argumen yang mana?
question.explanation: Kalimat (C) memberi **fakta dengan angka** dari tempat yang nyata: kalimat ini menunjukkan bahwa alasan (B) benar, jadi ini **evidence** (bukti). (B) adalah alasan (menjawab **mengapa**, dengan **because**), dan (D), dengan **Critics say**, adalah argumen tandingan.

steps.title: Mengenali bias
steps.text: Sebuah teks bisa berisi fakta yang benar semua dan tetap bias. Biasnya ada di pilihan kata dan pilihan fakta.
steps.body:
**Bias** = penulis condong ke satu sisi. Enam tandanya:
- **Loaded words** (kata bermuatan): a **reckless** plan (nekat: negatif) / a **bold** plan (berani: positif) / a new plan (netral); slashed vs reduced; claims vs says
- **Bukti sepihak**: hanya fakta yang membantu
- **Siapa yang membiayai**: penelitian perusahaan gula bilang gula aman
- **Angka yang dipilih-pilih** (cherry-picked): hanya bulan terbaik
- **Sampel kecil**: kami bertanya ke 15 pengguna
- **Berlindung di balik nama besar**: aktor terkenal bilang produknya manjur; "experts agree" (ahli yang mana?)

steps.title: Buat jadi netral
steps.text: Sekarang tulis ulang kalimat yang bias dengan kata-kata netral. Buang penilaiannya, pertahankan faktanya.

question.solution: The plan will reduce funding for libraries.
question.prompt: Baca: 'The reckless plan will slash funding for libraries.' Susun kata-katanya untuk memberi fakta yang sama dengan kata-kata netral.
question.explanation: **reckless** (penilaian negatif: nekat) hilang, dan **slash** (memangkas banyak, sembarangan) menjadi **reduce** (mengurangi) yang netral. Faktanya tetap sama: ada rencana, dan dana untuk perpustakaan berkurang.

steps.title: Membaca kritis
steps.text: Keterampilan terakhir: apakah buktinya benar-benar mendukung klaimnya? Pembaca yang kritis bertanya dulu sebelum percaya.
steps.body:
- **Korelasi ≠ sebab-akibat**: penjualan payung dan kasus DBD sama-sama naik di musim hujan. Payung tidak menyebabkan DBD: hujanlah penyebab keduanya.
- **Sampel**: berapa orang, dan siapa? 15 teman ≠ semua orang Indonesia.
- **Apa yang tidak ada?** Dibandingkan dengan apa? Bulan-bulan lainnya? Efek sampingnya?
- **Fakta atau opini?** Fakta bisa dicek; opini adalah penilaian.
Tanyakan: **Siapa yang menulis? Untuk siapa? Siapa yang membayar? Apa yang tidak disebut?** "A study shows…" bukan bukti pasti: satu penelitian hanya mengindikasikan.

steps.title: Apakah itu cerita lengkapnya?
steps.text: Siaran pers dari pemerintah kota. Baca judulnya, lalu tanyakan: apakah angka ini cerita lengkapnya?

options: It uses only the best week, so the number may be cherry-picked.
40,000 passengers is too small a sample.
question.prompt: Baca: 'NEW BUS LINE A HUGE SUCCESS. In its best week, during the school holidays, Bandung's new Line 9 carried 40,000 passengers. The city had planned for 30,000 a week.' Pemerintah kota belum mengumumkan angka untuk minggu-minggu lainnya. Apa masalah utama dari buktinya?
question.explanation: Penulis memilih **minggu terbaik**, saat liburan sekolah, dan minggu-minggu lainnya **tidak ada**: contoh khas angka yang dipilih-pilih (cherry-picked). 40.000 penumpang bukan sampel kecil, dan teksnya tidak bilang satu hal menyebabkan hal lain.
displayOptions: Hanya memakai minggu terbaik, jadi datanya mungkin dipilih agar terlihat bagus.

steps.title: Rangkuman
steps.text: Ini rangkuman untuk disimpan di dekat laporan, kontrak atau artikel opini berikutnya yang kamu baca.

steps.title: Baca dan tonton lagi
steps.text: Mau latihan lagi? Artikel C1 dari British Council LearnEnglish yang mempertanyakan apakah statistik mendukung pandangan kita tentang dunia, dan video Crash Course tentang cara membedakan bukti yang kuat dari yang lemah.
